chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Mubārak, from Zakariyyā ibn Ādam, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a drop of wine or intoxicating nabīdh that falls into a pot containing much meat and much broth. He said: “The broth is to be poured out, or fed to the أهل الذمة, or to the dog; and as for the meat, wash it and eat it.”
I said: What if blood fell into it? He said: “The fire consumes the blood, if Allah, Most High, wills.”
I said: Then if wine or nabīdh falls into dough, or blood? He said: “It is spoiled.”
I said: May I sell it to the Jews and the Christians and make it clear to them? He said: “Yes, for they deem its drinking lawful.”
I said: And is al-fuqāʿ in that same category if it falls into any of that? He said: “I dislike eating it if it falls into any of my food.”
As for what has been narrated regarding the permissibility of salat (prayer) in a garment that wine or an intoxicant has touched, it is to be understood as issued under taqiyyah, likewise.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: prudential dissimulation; a principle used to interpret reports that appear to permit salat (prayer) in affected clothing
key_terms.اللَّحْمُ: meat; the solid food that is to be washed and then eaten
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: al-fuqāʿ; a fermented beverage mentioned in comparison to wine and nabīdh
key_terms.خَمْرٍ: wine; an intoxicating liquid treated here as contaminating food and clothing
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood; treated here differently in cooked food and in dough
key_terms.عَجِينٍ: dough; if contaminated by wine, nabīdh, or blood, it is ruled spoiled
key_terms.مَرَقُ: broth; the liquid in the pot that is ordered to be poured out or given away
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ مُسْكِرٍ: intoxicating nabīdh; a fermented drink that carries the same ruling context here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if wine, intoxicating nabīdh, blood, or al-fuqāʿ falls into food or onto clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on food and garments affected by wine, intoxicating nabīdh, blood, and al-fuqāʿ. It distinguishes between broth, meat, and dough in cases of contamination, and it also notes that some contrary reports about salat (prayer) in affected clothing are to be interpreted as taqiyyah.
